purpose: Mitapivat is used to treat a rare blood condition called pyruvate kinase (PK) deficiency, which causes red blood cells to break down too quickly, leading to anemia. It helps reduce the symptoms of this condition, such as fatigue, weakness, and the need for blood transfusions. It is approved for adults with this inherited disorder.
how_it_works: In PK deficiency, red blood cells lack a working version of an enzyme called pyruvate kinase, which they need to produce energy and stay healthy. Without enough of this enzyme, red blood cells become fragile and break apart too soon. Mitapivat works by activating and boosting the pyruvate kinase enzyme so red blood cells can make more energy, live longer, and stay healthier.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include decreased levels of certain hormones (which can affect male fertility), increased uric acid levels in the blood, back pain, joint pain, and sleep problems. Some people may also notice changes in their testosterone levels.
warnings: Do not stop taking this medication suddenly without talking to your doctor, as stopping abruptly can cause your red blood cells to break down rapidly and worsen your anemia. This medication may affect hormone levels, including testosterone, and could impact fertility in men. Women who are pregnant or planning to become pregnant should discuss the risks with their doctor. Regular blood tests will be needed to monitor your response to the medication.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 5 mg taken by mouth twice a day with or without food. Your doctor may increase your dose over time to 20 mg twice a day, depending on how well it is working and how you are tolerating it. Try to take it at the same times each day for best results.
